nodes.recap: chapter header + arrival at the head of the stair, through the veils; companions present but frozen, not absent
nodes.text:
-------------------------------
|          CHAPTER 22          |
-------------------------------


$CYou come off the last step, through the veils, and into a hall
that is elliptical, and enormous, and quiet.##

Columns and marble climb the wall all the way round you toward a
high, far dome, open at its centre, and the light comes down through
that opening and through the tall windows together, oblique and
banded, gold and white.##

The floor is marble polished until it is a mirror, and crossing it
is like crossing glass, and you come to a stop out in the middle of
it, at one focus of that great ellipse, without having decided to.##

Your friends have followed you up the steps and are somewhere behind
you, you are dimly aware of that much.##

Every access is veiled, four in all, hung with drapes so vast and so
weightless at the same time that they give away every movement of
the air, and it is the drapes that take your attention now, because
the ones on the left-hand entrance have just stopped moving.##

Everything stops.# The drapes, the light, the air itself.# And your
friends, still standing where they stood, as if something had reached
into the room and turned all of them to statues.##

And you turn sharply, feeling the presence in the hall before
you have seen anything at all.##

nodes.recap: the armored warrior is already standing at the far focus, gives the name Saberinne, attacks; the name arrives as a telepathic Dialogue line, which prints no speaker name on screen, so sex is still not disclosed - the reveal is node 12
nodes.text:
$CA figure is standing at the hall's other focus, the far point
of the ellipse, facing you through the slits of a great helm.#
Not walking toward you, not arriving: already there, as though
the room had always held that shape and you had only now turned
around to find it.##

The armor is old, older than anything you have seen on this planet,
and that is not a small claim.# Full plate of a dark greenish metal,
greaves and gauntlets and breastplate and gorget, and that great
helm closing over everything above the shoulders, so that not one
inch of what is underneath is left uncovered.##

Two swords hang from the gauntleted hands, points downward, inert
at the hips: long, slightly curved sabers, gold handles, blades
the color of blue glass, an impossible material that is neither
steel nor crystal but something with the properties of both.#
They hang in a grip that is more frightening than any guard.##

And you feel the force that comes off that armored shape, the force
of the mind inside it as much as of the body, pressing at you
across the marble.##

A thousand voices ring in your head at once, and you almost believe
you see the air between you tremble with the flow of that energy:#

dialogues.line: I am Saberinne.
dialogues.comment:
##

Before you can register a single syllable of that, the figure comes
at you, without a sound in all that enormous hall except the sound
of armored feet on marble.

nodes.recap: Phase 1 - the exchange, a winnable Fight. Victory = parry, kick, drop, the warrior waits rather than strike a downed man, his feint read and countered, transition into phase 2 (unwinnable retreat). Defeat = sarcastic roast, engine returns to node 1.
nodes.text:
$CBlind instinct draws your sword from its scabbard.##

There is no room in your mind, in this instant, for the fact
that you are a university student from Earth who has never
properly held a weapon in your life.# There is only your own
movement and the warrior's, the sabers cutting the air fast
and silent, and the sword in your two hands that has been part
of you for so many months now that it answers before you think.##

You feel every molecule of air you displace.# Instead of trying
to flee, or simply parry, you hurl yourself at the warrior with
the same mad abandon that is coming at you.##

Without a sound you drive the blade forward at the moment
of impact, a blow so committed it very nearly throws you off
your own feet.

encounter.victorymessage:
$CBut the warrior meets your lunge with lightning speed, one saber
turning your blade aside, then pirouettes in place and puts a boot
into you that sends you tumbling across the marble for several
metres.##

Your sword clatters away from you.##

You scramble up and snatch it back.# Your opponent is waiting,
still, patient, unhurried.# There will be no blow struck at a man
who is on the ground and disarmed.##

This time you move first.# You run at that waiting figure, feint
low, and throw your weight into a committed slide meant to catch
the warrior off balance.# But a heartbeat before you commit to it,
your opponent has already stepped aside, unbothered, as if the feint
had been read before you had finished thinking it.##

You plant the sword's tip against the marble and drag yourself
back to your feet, the blade still skidding, throwing up a trail
of sparks that leave no mark on that impossible floor.##

There is no ground left to give away, and you both know it.
encounter.defeatmessage:
$CThe warrior reads the opening a half-second before you commit
to it, and this time there is no scramble back to your feet,
no second chance declined.$d##


-- GAME OVER --#


$DYou charged a full suit of ancient plate carrying two swords,
with a blade you personally have been swinging for about three
months.# Whatever is inside that helm did not even change
its breathing.# It will not remember your name either.# Try again.

nodes.recap: phase 2 opens - losing ground begins, first desperate tactic (unwinnable, both options converge)
nodes.text:
$CThe warrior comes on again before you have fully found your
footing.##

There is no opening anywhere in that armor, only the dizzying,
absolute sense of an opponent already standing where you are about
to be.# Twice you feel it happen: an idea forms half a second
before you act on it, and by the time your blade moves it has
already been answered.##

You have to try something.

choices.desc: Meet the sabers blade for blade, force against force.
Break the rhythm, cut in from an angle left unguarded.

nodes.recap: phase 2a - brute force option, loses ground, converges
nodes.text:
$CYou throw your whole weight behind the next exchange, sparks
raining in sheets between your blades.##

It buys you nothing.# The warrior simply lets your strength carry
past, and you give a half-step back just to keep your feet under you.

nodes.recap: phase 2a - angle option, loses ground, converges
nodes.text:
$CYou veer wide, aiming for the gap you would swear you saw
at the armored hip a heartbeat ago.##

The gap is not there anymore.# It was never really there;
it was closed before you had finished thinking of it, and you give
ground instead, a half-step back just to keep your feet under you.

nodes.recap: phase 2 second exchange - wall approaching, second desperate tactic (unwinnable, both options converge)
nodes.text:
$CThe hall keeps turning behind you, though you cannot spare
a glance to see how much of it is left.##

You are fighting as you have never fought in your life,
and you are still losing.# One more idea, then.# Anything.

choices.desc: Feint low, then reverse the blade at the last instant.
Abandon finesse. Throw everything into one overhead cut.

nodes.recap: phase 2b - feint reversal, loses more ground, converges to the wall
nodes.text:
$CYou drop low, and at the very last instant twist the blade
back the other way, the kind of move that should buy at least
a heartbeat of confusion.##

It buys you nothing.# The warrior is already turning with you,
as if the reversal had been read in the set of your shoulders
before you had committed to it, and the wall is closer now than
it was a moment ago.

nodes.recap: phase 2b - overhead cut, loses more ground, converges to the wall
nodes.text:
$CYou abandon caution entirely and swing everything you have
into one committed, two-handed cut, the kind of blow you cannot
take back once it starts.##

The warrior steps inside it before it lands, close enough that
the blade never finds anything but air, and you stumble past,
the wall closer now than it was a moment ago.

nodes.recap: the faceless-helm beat from the source (will he ever see that face, and how many could say they had and were still alive), then back against the wall - lost - determination rises into the Surge
nodes.text:
$CYou keep turning the sabers away, one exchange and then
another, and from behind the slits of that great helm the faceless
warrior watches you do it.# You find yourself wondering whether
you will ever see the face under there, and how many, in fact,
could claim they had, and were still alive to claim it...##

Suddenly you find the wall at your back.# Your right hand
still holds the sword; your left presses flat to the cold marble
behind you.# The tip of the right-hand saber finds your throat.#
A clear gesture.##

It was only a few instants, and yet it was an eternity.# You have
fought as you never imagined anyone could, and you have lost.##

But you cannot accept it.# You cannot let it end like this.#
You think again of everything you have been through, of everything
you have seen and done alongside the friends who would give
their lives for one another without a second thought.##

It cannot end here.##

You grip the sword's hilt, and something in your chest, old
and familiar, the same thing that once tore a door out of its frame
at the bottom of the sea, begins to burn.

nodes.recap: Phase 3 - the release. Surge instance 4, tuned generous: fast and enormous, not hard. No failurechildid: a Surge here is never a Game Over, the player simply gathers it again.
nodes.text:
$CThe blade rests, patient, against your throat.##

You scream.

challenge.successmessage:
$CThe sword loses its weight in your hand, and then it is not
in your hand at all: it tears free and flashes upward, faster
than sight, and strikes the helm with a force so tremendous
that for one instant the glare of wounded metal blinds the two
of you alike.##

The helm spins away, ringing, down the staircase you climbed
to get here.##

The light returns.
challenge.failuremessage:
$CThe scream catches in your throat and the fury slips through
your fingers.# But the wall is still at your back, and there is
nowhere left to fall to.##

You grit your teeth, and gather it again.

nodes.recap: the unmasking - Saberinne revealed; her name is now a spoken Dialogue line, and the recognition stays at the source's compass (she recognised the voice, she had found her)
nodes.text:
$CTime resumes.##

The armor seems to breathe, then to recede, drawing back into
itself until it is gone, and what stands under it is superb beyond
anything you have seen before or will ever see again.##

It is a woman.##

She is beautiful in a way that has no relation to age, because age
has not touched her.# Not young, not old, but $Woutside of time$C
entirely, as though time long ago gave up trying to find purchase
on her and simply moved on.##

Blonde curls fall around her face and down her back, spilling over
a white dress that reveals a perfect figure.# Her eyes are the color
of the sea at a depth where the sun still reaches, green and clear,
full of warmth and an even greater strength.##

She looks at you with those eyes, and she smiles.##

dialogues.line: I am Saberinne.
dialogues.comment:
She says it with a certain satisfaction, projecting that same
warmth directly into your mind.##

You know that voice.##

You have found her.

nodes.recap: companions react - Efeliah and Smiurl prostrate themselves, Saberinne corrects them, invites everyone to the portico

dialogues.precomment:
Your companions, it turns out, had been standing behind you
the whole time, and had noticed nothing at all of the duel.#
They are only now recovering from the stupor of the arrival,
looking around the hall in various states of wonder.##

Efeliah is the first to recover.# When she understands what kind
of person stands before her, she drops to the floor, prostrating
herself as though before a goddess.# Smiurl copies her at once,
his skin flooding a reverent blue-violet.# Theo and Corolla
stay on their feet, staring.##

Saberinne looks at Efeliah with a warmth that is also a correction.
dialogues.line:
Rise.# I am not what you think.#
I am a human being, the same as all of you.
dialogues.comment: She says it without vanity, and without false modesty.

dialogues.line: But...
dialogues.comment: Ef hesitates, still on her knees.

dialogues.line:
Come, follow me.# Make yourselves comfortable under the portico.#
I believe I owe you a great many explanations.
dialogues.comment:
She turns toward the northern entrance, and they follow her
down a corridor of equal splendor.

nodes.recap: corridor, terrace, slavery line, the meal, Saberinne's gaze, she begins to speak

dialogues.precomment:
Frescoed ceilings, marble walls and tall windows pour oblique
light across the floor as you walk, and your companions crane
their necks, dazzled by so much splendor.# You barely notice
any of it.# You and Saberinne walk ahead of the others, looking
into each other's eyes, exchanging thoughts entirely impenetrable
even to Efeliah.##

The corridor opens onto a wide, covered terrace, framed
by climbing plants tended with obvious care, descending toward
the gardens by two broad staircases.# A small table is already set.#
Servants bring a cart of refreshments: a young man and a young woman,
both smiling easily.
dialogues.line:
I do not tolerate slavery in this city.#
Work in this palace is a privilege, given freely.
dialogues.comment:
She says it briefly, because it is simply how things are.#
The two bow and withdraw.##

You eat under her gaze, which seems to reach past your faces
and into your minds, and further still.# After a while she stops
watching the others and settles on you alone, chin resting
on one closed hand.# It is, unmistakably, the look of someone
in love, and you are helplessly, completely enchanted by it.##

When everyone has finished eating, Saberinne begins to speak.

nodes.recap: revelation - she perceived Kriss's arrival, it was prophesied

dialogues.line:
Kriss, I perceived your presence from the very day you arrived
on Noi-Hert, born from the deepest fiber of our own universe.#
I knew of your coming.# It was prophesied.# And even if it hadn't
been, all of this would have happened just the same.
dialogues.comment: She holds your eyes as she says it.

replies.line: How could you possibly know that?

nodes.recap: revelation - parallel universes, not time travel; two factors, his mind the greater one; additional dimensions

dialogues.line:
You come from a universe parallel to this one.# You did not
travel through your own space, nor your own time.# Two things
made the crossing possible: the lightning that struck near you,
in a storm of unusual proportions that altered the energy
around your home and your own mind.# And, far more important,
your mind itself.
dialogues.comment: She pauses, as if to let that settle.

dialogues.line:
As you can all see, even now, it lies as far outside the ordinary
as mine does.# This universe, as you were already told
at Seer's Rock, holds additional dimensions.# They allow minds
to exchange more than words, and, in the rarest of them,
to bend the ordinary laws of matter.
dialogues.comment: She fixes her eyes on you.

dialogues.line: Yours is one of those minds.

replies.line: What does that even mean, bend matter?

nodes.recap: revelation - Ef's shielded aside overheard, the word telekinesis, the escalation (Oxengutter night, Ayonn's Projector, the submarine door), the mountain line

dialogues.precomment: Efeliah makes a small, involuntary sound.
dialogues.line:
So that's what the structures are.# The ones I always felt
in you, but could never name.

Exactly.# You would call it, a little imprecisely, telekinesis.#
Those circuits were never used, in the whole course of your life,
because they were simply useless in your own universe.# When you
arrived on this planet, though, the energy of your mind began
pressing against them on its own.

The night you saved Smiurl from the Sgozza-Buoi, the nearness
of Efeliah's mind pushed a massive dose of raw feeling into you,
and it threw your whole mental balance into disarray for a while.#
It was like flooring a cold engine: your mind overheated,
and very nearly damaged itself.

But that night mattered enormously.# From that evening on,
access to those structures was unlocked.# It is what let you reach
me through Ayonn's Projector, among other things.# And you gave
off another discharge entirely when you tore that door apart,
in the mutants' colony under the sea.

Since then, hour by hour, day by day, your potential has grown
enormously.# Would you believe me if I told you that you could
move a mountain now, if you only wanted to?
dialogues.comment:
She watches your face, and answers her own question
before you fully can.

dialogues.line:
No, I can see that you wouldn't.# And that, precisely,
is what keeps you from actually managing it.

nodes.recap: the garden, the siege - no army by constitution, dozens of Hordes allied, her life bound to the city

dialogues.line: Come.# Let's walk in the garden.
dialogues.comment:
You follow her down the staircase into the palace gardens,
fountains playing, flowers and trees bending in a warm breeze,
Saberinne walking barefoot on the grass.##

After a few minutes she sighs, and speaks again with an infinite
sadness in her voice.

dialogues.line:
My city, a thousand years old, is under siege.# It risks
annihilation.# Everything you glimpsed from the hills risks
being wiped away for good.

It has no army.# That is part of its constitution.# Our isolation
on this distant southern continent, and our walls, have always
been enough against the sporadic hordes that dared push this far.

It is no longer enough.# Dozens of Hordes have struck an alliance
to seize the city and its wealth, the only wealth of any kind,
economic or technological, left intact anywhere on this planet.

Defending this city is my life.# It carries my own name,
and for as long as it has lived, I have lived.# If it were
destroyed, it would mean the destruction of my own soul as well.
dialogues.comment: They stop, reflecting on those words.

nodes.recap: Corolla's millennia question - her age, the body as product of the mind, her soul drawing on her people and the planet's core

dialogues.line: That would mean you have lived for millennia...
dialogues.comment:
Incredulous.# Saberinne does not answer right away.# She walks
a few more paces barefoot on the grass, then stops, and turns.

dialogues.line:
Does it seem strange to you, that I have kept my life and my
beauty after all this time?# The body is only the product
of the mind.# A perfect knowledge and use of it spares the body
from carrying the marks of decay.# And my soul draws its energy
from every one of Saberinne's people, and, in small part,
from the forces buried in the heart of this planet.

replies.line: Say nothing, and let her go on.

nodes.recap: she knew the Master; Kriss raises Elder Long's legend of the golden goddess; Saberinne is genuinely surprised - the one thing she does not know; she asks to speak privately

dialogues.line: It's incredible...

dialogues.precomment: She answers your own thoughts before you can voice them.
dialogues.line: I knew the Master.
dialogues.comment: A pause, for all of you to absorb it.

replies.line: Wait. The legend Elder Long told us.
Ask her about Long's dream of the goddess.

dialogues.line:
The Master dreamed of a golden goddess, who told him
to expect our coming to the Rock.# Elder Long told us the story
himself.

dialogues.precomment: She tilts her head, genuinely surprised.
dialogues.line:
That's funny.# I knew nothing about that.# I passed on to him
what knowledge the few years we had together allowed.# Your
community is the product of that meeting of ours.# But a dream
foretelling your arrival?# That is something he built entirely
on his own.# Remarkable, given the circumstances, I grant you.
dialogues.comment: A silence, everyone turning that over.

dialogues.precomment: She seems to hesitate, then sighs.
dialogues.line: Kriss, I would like to speak with you privately.
dialogues.comment:
She says it without apology, because she does not need one.##

$c<<I would not refuse for anything in the world.>>$C

nodes.recap: the hedge maze - wordless soulmate communion

dialogues.precomment:
The others exchange glances.# Corolla opens her mouth, then
closes it again; something in Saberinne's expression is not
quite an instruction, but carries the weight of one.
dialogues.line: We'll be by the fountain.
dialogues.comment:
Flat.# Efeliah respectfully withdraws even her mental presence,
which, in any case, would be useless here.

dialogues.precomment:
She leads you through the gardens to a hedge maze, along passages
of perfect green, until they open onto a small clearing
at the center: a stone bench, a fountain playing quietly,
flowers growing close to the water.##

You sit.# Your mind and your heart feel ready to crack open,
so many thoughts and feelings crowd into you at once that no
single word can form.##

She raises one finger to her lips, smiling.
dialogues.line: Don't say anything.
dialogues.comment:
She whispers it softly, into your mind.##

And so you don't.##

You sit facing each other, and your eyes find hers, and what
happens then is not conversation, in any form you have a name for.#
You are looking directly into each other's minds, past every
surface, and what is there is exact.# Perfectly complementary.#
Two things built to find each other.##

No words.# No images.# The language is emotion itself.# Every
neuron you have vibrates in time with every thought she has.#
You can feel her breathing on your face, counting the molecules
of air between you in a time that stretches like honey.# Her hands
find yours, meeting in the middle.##

The fountain stops playing with the water.# A single bird, alone
in the sky above the hedge, sings.

nodes.recap: return to the others - Corolla's explosion, Ef's anxiety, kindred souls explained, Ef's shielded thought overheard

dialogues.precomment:
You walk back to the others, arm in arm, well into the afternoon.##

Saberinne takes her leave with the same composure she carries
in everything, though she holds your gaze a half-second longer
than anyone else's - a farewell only you can read.##

The moment she is gone, Corolla says, loudly, without the smallest
concern about being overheard:
dialogues.line:
Will you tell us what the hell she was saying to you
for all that time?!
Nothing.# We didn't exchange a single word.

dialogues.precomment:
An uncomfortable silence.# Then Efeliah steps closer, her face
carrying something between concern and wonder.
dialogues.line:
Kriss... something has changed in you.# Profoundly.#
I almost don't recognize you...
Are you alright?
dialogues.comment:
He looks from Ef to you, already anxious at his friends'
expressions.

dialogues.line: I believe so.
dialogues.comment:
He says it without turning from the window where he has been
watching the garden.# The others look at him, not understanding.

dialogues.line: Do you know the concept of kindred souls?
dialogues.comment:
Efeliah explains it to the others, and after a moment
you go on.

dialogues.line:
I stopped believing in things like that when I was a child.#
The facts have now shown me I was wrong.# My mind and Saberinne's
are perfectly complementary.# They can merge into a single entity,
without any resistance...

In the garden, you were exchanging thoughts.# Looking into
each other's minds.
Yes.
Are you certain of that?
dialogues.comment: Sharp.

dialogues.line: Yes.
He's lying.
dialogues.comment:
She thinks it at Corolla, shielding it out of habit, then looks
up and finds you already watching her.

replies.line: Hold her gaze, and let her work it out.

dialogues.line:
How is that even possible?# So far, only Saberinne has ever
been able to see through my shields!
dialogues.comment: She stares at you, stunned.

nodes.recap: Kriss reveals his life is bound to Saberinne's; Corolla's devastating quiet reaction

dialogues.line:
We are one thing, now.# Two faces of the same coin.# My life
is hers, her city is mine, and our hearts, our breath, have become
one and the same...
dialogues.comment:
Corolla drops onto the edge of the nearest bed and stares
at the ceiling.

dialogues.line: What's happened to you...
dialogues.comment: She murmurs it, half to herself, staring into empty space.

replies.line: Put a hand on her shoulder, and say nothing.

dialogues.precomment: You put a hand on her shoulder.
dialogues.line:
You are still my best friends.# The finest companions anyone
has ever had.# But my life, from now on, is bound to Saberinne's.#
In every place.# In every time.

nodes.recap: night falls - quarters - retire to rooms - chapter end
nodes.text:
$CWith that, you each retire to your rooms.##

Saberinne has arranged everything: quiet quarters, warm water,
clean clothes, a silence that is not the silence of a besieged
city but of one that has decided, somewhere deep down, that it
means to survive the morning.##

You wash, change, and stand a long while at the window, looking
out over the gardens in the day's last light, over the walls,
over the campfires of an army that has no idea what is waiting
for it.##

$c<<Tomorrow.>>$C##

Sleep takes you before you finish the thought.
